title: Establish red-green TDD with a runner and a first real test
description:
Adopt red-green TDD for Number Up, independent of the TypeScript migration. This is the prerequisite that makes the migration safe, and it pays off whether or not that migration happens.

Scope:
- Pick a runner. Zero-dependency-to-minimal matters here; the repo currently has no package.json at all, so this bead is where one appears. node:test plus node:assert is the lowest-friction option given Node 26 is already installed and requires no new dependency at all; justify the choice over vitest/jest on the grounds that a browser prototype with no build step should not acquire a heavy test toolchain.
- Write the first test red before any implementation change. engine.js is the target: the pure rule registry and createEngine have no DOM dependency, so they are directly testable today, before any migration.
- Cover the semantics recorded in the memory number-up-eval-rule-semantics-current-candidate-numeric: numeric tiles replace and set pending, operator tiles apply to (currentNumber, pending), operator chains act as verbs, operators with no pending operand yield an invalid result. Also cover each failure rule boundary (DOWN, flat, invalid) since notUp.failed depends on the check order at engine.js:69-71.
- Add a typecheck/test script convention and wire both into the session-close quality gates described in AGENTS.md.
- Document the red-green loop in AGENTS.md so future sessions follow it without being asked.

Acceptance:
- At least one test written and observed failing before its implementation existed, with the failure recorded on the bead.
- npm test (or the chosen command) passes and is documented in AGENTS.md.
- Tests run from a clean checkout with a single documented command and no manual setup.

Notes: Deliberately scoped to engine.js. Do not attempt DOM coverage of main.js here — it has no DOM test harness and building one is a separate decision. Test the pure logic first; that is where the bugs that matter live.
acceptance_criteria: Test runner installed, first test written red-then-green against engine.js, documented command in AGENTS.md, wired into quality gates.
notes:
Runner: node:test + node:assert (Node v26.10.0, zero deps, no install). Justification: no-build-step browser prototype opening via file:// must not acquire heavy vitest/jest toolchain; stdlib runner runs from clean checkout with single command 'npm test' (node --test test/), no node_modules needed.

RED (observed before implementation change): mutated test to naive expectation 'operator with no pending leaves Number unchanged' (assert ev.valid==true, result==5 for attempt(5,'up','+')). npm/node --test failed as expected: 13 pass / 1 fail. Failing test: 'operators with no pending operand yield an invalid result' at test/engine.test.js:45 — AssertionError ERR_ASSERTION false !== true (actual:false expected:true, operator strictEqual). Confirms test is red-capable: engine correctly returns valid=false result=null for pending==null (engine.js:53).

GREEN: restored correct expectation (valid==false, result==null); no engine change needed — test-correctness fix only. engine.js eval/notUp semantics already match memory number-up-eval-rule-semantics-current-candidate-numeric. npm test now 14 pass / 0 fail. Coverage: numeric REPLACE+pending, operator apply (current,pending), verb chains (+ + +), no-pending invalid, floor passthrough, notUp order invalid/DOWN/flat (engine.js:69-71), end-to-end DOWN/flat/invalid fail + UP pass, createEngine wiring/fallback/history.

Files: test/engine.test.js (new), package.json (new, test script), AGENTS.md Build&Test (runner + red-green loop + quality gate). Verified: npm test green, no node_modules present (clean-checkout single command). No DOM coverage of main.js per scope.
close_reason: Red observed+recorded (1 fail on naive no-pending expectation), green 14/0 via test-correctness fix (no engine change), npm test documented in AGENTS.md, single-command clean checkout verified (no node_modules). Tree left dirty for coordinator.

title: Isolated failure rule: provisional 'NUMBER NOT UP' semantics
description: Open design question — do NOT quietly settle it. Implement one provisional, isolated rule (candidate: a superposition that does not make Number go UP ends the run) in its own swappable spot next to the collision rule. Candidates from the plan: decrease→death, fail-to-increase→death, invalid result→death, non-numeric/undefined→death, up-undefined-domain→death, something else. On failure: show clearly WHY (which hypothesis of failure fired) so play can judge it. Deep hypothesis being explored: failure is not health-zero, it is NUMBER NOT UP. We don't know yet.
acceptance_criteria: Failure predicate is a single isolated function/binding; changing the death semantics requires no restructuring; the run end states which failure condition fired and offers restart.
close_reason: engine.js FAILURE_RULES isolates the predicate: notUp (provisional: run ends when Number goes DOWN, stays flat, or becomes invalid — reason string states which fired) and none. ?fail= param and F key swap at runtime; run-over screen names the condition and offers R restart. Verified: DOWN/flat/invalid all fail with distinct reasons; none never fails.

title: Isolated collision engine: superpose(current, tile) → result + event record
description: Core operation conceptually: superpose(currentNumber, destinationTile) → result. Must be a tiny isolated module trivially replaceable — no restructuring to try a different interpretation. Ship candidate rules side by side, NOT one 'correct' answer: replacement, addition, operator evaluation (tile operator applies to current Number and... something), and leave room for other interpretations. Rules selectable without code changes where cheap (e.g. ?rule= query param). Record an event per move: {turn, direction, oldNumber, destinationTile, result, delta, wentUp, valid}; keep a cheap run history for comparing rules. Do not assume operators (+ − × ÷) are conventional or that Number+Number must mean arithmetic.
acceptance_criteria: superpose() lives in its own file/section; switching rule interpretation requires changing one binding (or a query param), nothing else; every move appends an event with the listed fields; history is retained in-memory.
close_reason: engine.js isolates superpose(currentNumber, tile, ctx) with three swappable candidate rules (replace/add/eval) plus URL param ?rule= and C key; event record {turn,direction,oldNumber,destinationTile,result,delta,wentUp,valid,failed,failReason} kept in in-memory history. 23 node assertions passed covering all rules, invalid results, and event fields.

title: Movement: dot IS the Number, keyboard input, move is the only verb
description: Player moves through the grid with arrow keys, numpad, and WASD. The dot is not a character on a number — it IS the current Number. Moving into an adjacent cell triggers the superposition event (engine issue handles the rule). Edges block movement (invalid, no event). No interact/attack/collect buttons, no other verbs.
acceptance_criteria: Arrow keys, numpad, and WASD move the dot; edges are blocked; each move into a tile produces a superposition event.
close_reason: Arrows, WASD, and numpad (2/4/6/8) move the dot; edges blocked with feedback; movement is the only verb. Verified via jsdom keypress simulation for all four input families.

acceptance_criteria: Opening index.html directly shows the 5×5 grid, center dot, current NUMBER 0, and message area.
close_reason: index.html + style.css + SVG grid built: three UI regions (status with NUMBER, world grid with distinct center dot, observation area), world data hand-authored in world.js, opens from file://. Verified via jsdom: grid renders 38 nodes, dot centered at 250,250, NUMBER 0 shown.

description: Runnable local prototype of the Number Up design laboratory (_the_beginning.md). Premise: the player is a central dot and the dot IS the current Number (start 0). title: Apply best-practice TypeScript to the work completed so far
description:
Retrofit the existing code to the TypeScript setup established in the parent bead, migrating behind the safety net the TDD bead provides.

Scope:
- Convert engine.js, world.js, main.js, gallery.js, variants.js from IIFE globals to ES modules, keeping the existing file boundaries.
- Run strict tsc across all of it and triage every diagnostic into: real bug, missing annotation, or intentional dynamic behaviour.
- The registry contracts are the highest-value typing target and should be typed explicitly: the superpose(currentNumber, tile, ctx) signature, the ctx.pending number|null mutation protocol threaded through engine.js:31,40,50 and read at 109,116, and the Ev event object built at engine.js:118-131.
- ev.result is number|null (engine.js:123) while notUp.failed does ev.result < ev.oldNumber at engine.js:70. That is safe only because ev.valid is checked first at line 69. Model it as a discriminated union on valid so the ordering invariant becomes structural rather than conventional.
- Do not restructure to satisfy the checker. The RULES / FAILURE_RULES isolation in engine.js and the VARIANTS registry in variants.js are deliberate design properties — adding a variant must remain one registry entry plus one notebook file.
- Verify ?debug=1 reports no new errors and that every debug entry point still works: ?world=gen&seed=N, ?rule=, ?fail=, ?variant=.
- Confirm the file:// smoke test still passes after each file converts.

Acceptance:
- tsc --noEmit passes strict with no unaccepted diagnostics; any accepted diagnostic is listed individually with its reason.
- The full test suite from the TDD bead still passes after migration.
- File:// smoke test recorded covering a move, a rule switch, a variant deep link, and a seeded world.
- Any real bug discovered during the retrofit is filed as its own bead if non-trivial.

Notes: This is the bead where untyped code meets a checker and defects surface. Fix real bugs, annotate the rest, and do not let type convenience drive design changes. The variant notebooks record intent; where code and intent diverge, record the divergence rather than silently reconciling it.
acceptance_criteria: Typecheck documented and passing or triaged; file:// smoke test recorded covering move, rule switch, and variant deep link.
notes:
Retrofit applied on top of parent Option B (src/*.ts ESM, dist IIFE, no commit).

TRIAGE (diagnostic → bucket + fix):
- play.ts unused Engine import (TS6133) → leftover → removed
- play.ts unused cycle(pool) param (TS6133) → leftover → dropped; cycle(order, key) only
- play.ts getElementById('…')! on els/svg → missing annotation / DOM contract → mustEl() null-throws
- play.ts params.get('variant')! → missing annotation → variantParam local
- play.ts genSeed! / WORLDS[key]! / rows[y]![x]! / DIRECTIONS[name]! / cycle()! / touches[0]! → noUncheckedIndexedAccess / missing annotation → union PlayWorld, optional chain, early return, Touch.item(0)
- play.ts showObservation(ev as MoveEvent) overload → missing annotation → split showBlocked vs showObservation
- play.ts as HTMLAnchorElement / as SVGElement / as Element / dataset.action index access → missing annotation → instanceof, typed createElementNS, getAttribute
- engine.ts RULES.eval! / FAILURE_RULES.notUp! (and noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature on Record<string,_>) → missing annotation → `satisfies Record<string, CollisionRule|FailureRule>` so keys are RuleName/FailureName; named() fallback, no bang
- engine.ts superpose(current, tile, ctx) vs bead currentNumber → missing annotation → param renamed currentNumber; MoveContext.pending number|null unchanged
- engine.ts ev.result number|null vs notUp result < oldNumber → real invariant, already modelled → ValidAttempt | InvalidAttempt on valid (see design note)
- world.ts OPS[i]! / rows[y]! → noUncheckedIndexedAccess → OPS as const + ?? '+'; skip undefined row
- gallery.ts getElementById/querySelector ! → mustEl + setText
- variants.ts id as VariantId → type guard isVariantId; VARIANT_ORDER derived from Object.keys so adding a variant stays one registry entry + one notebook
- tsconfig noUnusedLocals/Parameters not enabled → enabled; tsc clean
- extra flags probed (noPropertyAccessFromIndexSignature, exactOptionalPropertyTypes, noImplicitReturns, noFallthroughCasesInSwitch): also clean, not enabled (not requested)
- Accepted diagnostics: none

DISCRIMINATED UNION: AttemptOutcome = ValidAttempt | InvalidAttempt on `valid`.
valid:true → result:number, delta:number, wentUp:boolean; valid:false → result/delta null, wentUp false.
notUp.failed checks !ev.valid first; afterwards ev.result is number so DOWN/flat compares are legal. Swap the checks → TS18047 (result possibly null). Check-order is structural. Tests still pin the messages. RULES/FAILURE_RULES isolation and VARIANTS shape unchanged.

DIVERGENCE (recorded, not reconciled): variants/accretion.md hypothesis still says "every number is bigger than the last" — that is replace/Becoming. add × notUp goes UP on any k>0; 0/sign is flat death. Gallery `how` matches code. Note added under accretion.md Feedback.

VERIFY: npm run verify green (tsc --noEmit; 14 tests; esbuild dist/play.js 25.9kb + dist/gallery.js 4.9kb). Bundles have zero import/export. Extra-strict probe also clean.

FILE:// SMOKE (jsdom 25, JSDOM.fromFile = file:// script load, /tmp/kilo/verify/file-verify.mjs, no page errors):

title: Configure this repo for best-practice TypeScript development
description:
Set up TypeScript for this repo. DECISION (from user): pursue real TypeScript type safety, not check-only. The file:// constraint is negotiable and no longer binding on the design.

VERIFIED (probed, not assumed): compiled TypeScript does NOT require a local host.
- Option A: tsc --module none emits per-file plain scripts with zero import/export. Verified to open over file://. Downside: emitted file order is coupled to the script tag order in play.html:60-63, and output goes stale relative to source.
- Option B (PREFERRED): author ES modules with normal import/export, bundle to a single IIFE via esbuild --format=iife --outfile. Verified the emitted bundle contains zero import/export statements and therefore runs over file://. This gives proper module structure in source without sacrificing file:// openability.

Scope:
- Go with Option B. Convert the globalThis.NumberUp* globals to real ES module imports/exports.
- Add package.json, tsconfig.json (strict), esbuild build script, and an index.html/play.html script tag pointing at the built bundle.
- Decide whether the bundle is committed or built in CI. Note the GitHub Pages workflow currently uploads path "." verbatim with no build step, so a non-committed bundle REQUIRES editing that workflow. Record the choice and its reason.
- Fix the stale-output hazard, which is the real cost of a build step on a prototype opened by double-click. At minimum, make the build cheap and fast enough that the wrong file is rarely debugged.
- Wire typecheck + test + build into the quality gates in AGENTS.md and document the commands there.

Acceptance:
- tsc --noEmit passes under strict mode.
- The built bundle opens and plays from file:// with no local server.
- AGENTS.md documents the posture, the build/typecheck/test commands, and whether the bundle is committed or CI-built.

Notes: Sequencing matters. The TDD bead (num-hsy) blocks this one — migrate behind a passing test suite, not in front of it. Where engine.js and variants.js registries use globalThis today, the modules become the natural type boundary.
acceptance_criteria: tsconfig + typecheck command present and documented; AGENTS.md records the TS posture and why a build step was rejected.
notes:
Option B implemented. Sources are TypeScript ES modules in src/ (engine, world, variants, play, gallery) with real imports/exports replacing all four globalThis.NumberUp* globals; esbuild bundles per page to dist/play.js + dist/gallery.js as IIFEs with zero import/export in output (verified by grep). tsconfig: strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + verbatimModuleSyntax + isolatedModules + allowImportingTsExtensions + noEmit; tsc --noEmit (typescript@7.0.2 native) passes clean. BUNDLE DECISION: committed (dist/ tracked). Reason: Pages workflow uploads path '.' verbatim with no build step and keeps that posture (file:// works from bare checkout with no Node); building in CI before uploading '.' would publish node_modules too (upload-pages-artifact v3 excludes only .git/.github — checked action source). Stale-output hazard covered two ways: build is ~2ms (esbuild 0.28.2), and pages.yml gained a guard step (npm ci + npm run build + git diff over dist/ fails the deploy when bundle is stale; rm -rf node_modules before artifact upload). FILE:// VERIFICATION: no local browser available (cached playwright chromium missing libasound.so.2, no sudo; firefox is an uninstalled snap shim), so verified with jsdom 25 in /tmp/kilo/verify (outside repo): JSDOM.fromFile loads play.html/index.html with script tags as local paths (the file:// loading model) — play.html boots, plays ArrowRight (Number 0→6 via eval rule, position 2,2→3,2), then ArrowDown ('1' → not up → RUN OVER); index.html renders 6 gallery cards; deep link ?variant=verbs hands over to play.html (vm check); zero page errors. Static gate: no import/export statements in either bundle. TESTS: test/engine.test.js converted from require(globalThis.NumberUpEngine) to ESM import of ../src/engine.ts (Node 26 strips types natively); same 14 tests, all green; npm test still zero-install. package.json: type=module, scripts test/typecheck/build/verify. AGENTS.md Build & Test + Architecture rewritten (posture, commands, committed-bundle reason, quality gate now npm run verify when src/test/html changed). Child bead num-7ez.1.1 remains for the full retrofit pass (main.js-era patterns like non-null assertions in play.ts els/side casts, noUnusedLocals/Parameters not yet enabled). Acceptance met: typecheck strict green, file:// plays verified, AGENTS.md documents posture/commands/bundle choice. Tree left dirty, nothing committed per instructions.
[preserved prior note] Blocking consideration: any solution requiring a bundler or ES modules violates the file:// constraint. [superseded by user decision: real TS over check-only, file:// negotiable; Option B chosen]
close_reason: Acceptance met: strict tsc clean, file:// plays verified, AGENTS.md documents posture/commands/committed-bundle choice. Full retrofit continues in child num-7ez.1.1.

title: Install Matt Pocock TypeScript skills
description:
Install the Matt Pocock TypeScript skill suite into this repo's agent skill directories so later beads can rely on them being available.

Scope:
- Locate the authoritative source of Matt Pocock's TypeScript skills (do NOT guess URLs; verify the repo/owner first) and confirm which skills it contains.
- Install the skills into the project-local skill dir (.agents/skills/ alongside the existing beads skill) and/or the global dir this setup prefers.
- Record the installed skill names and their intended trigger conditions in the bead notes so the next bead can reference them by name.
- Ensure no repo files are overwritten; the existing beads skill must survive.

Acceptance:
- The skills are present on disk in a directory the agent runtime actually loads (verify the load path, not just that files exist).
- Each installed skill's name and purpose is recorded on the bead.

Notes: This repo currently has no TypeScript and no build step (plain <script> tags, globals, must open via file://). Installing skills is a prerequisite for bead 2, not a claim that a TS migration is already in flight.
acceptance_criteria: Matt Pocock TypeScript skills present in a runtime-loaded skill directory, names/purposes recorded on bead, existing beads skill untouched.
notes: Source verified (not guessed): https://github.com/mattpocock/skills — Matt Pocock's own repo, "Skills for Real Engineers", commit d81f3a1 (v1.3, 2026-09-29); confirmed via web search + README. title: Four experiment worlds A–D, switchable
description: Hand-authored tiny worlds, selectable via query param/key, no generation: A — Number+Number: numbers only; question: what interaction between two Numbers feels intrinsically interesting? B — Number+Operator: introduce + − × ÷; question: is an operator a thing you collide with or a verb you invoke? C — UP vs DOWN: authored layout where different movement choices give different numeric outcomes; question: does the player start thinking 'how do I make Number go UP'? D — Failure: situations where Number can go down, stay flat, go invalid; exercise the failure semantics; question: does failure feel like a consequence of the premise or a bolted-on rule? World data stays in the one obvious place so worlds are trivially editable.
acceptance_criteria: All four worlds are reachable and playable; switching worlds needs no code edit; each world is a small hand-authored grid in world data.
close_reason: world.js WORLDS: full (mixed), a (numbers only), b (operators), c (UP vs DOWN choices), d (failure situations with ÷0, ×0, flat moves). N key cycles, ?world= param selects; all verified playable in jsdom; no code edits needed to switch.

Debug mode (toggle key or ?debug param — no code changes): verbose detail — move direction, old/new number, delta, tile, rule used, turn index, recent history. Verbosity easy to turn down later.
acceptance_criteria: A toggle switches concise ↔ verbose modes at runtime without editing code; verbose mode shows the event-record fields.
close_reason: Message area shows per-move observation (You moved X / SUPERPOSITION / operands / Result / Number went UP). / key or ?debug=1 toggles verbose mode with full event-record history lines and rule/world/fail labels, no code changes. Verified in jsdom.

title: Superposition animation: visibly show current + destination → result
description: Never silently replace one number with another. On each collision, visibly interact the two values: current Number + destination flow together and the resulting Number emerges. Fast enough not to impede play, clear enough to see causality (order of a few hundred ms). The point: make 'what happened to Number?' perceptually obvious, including whether it went UP.
acceptance_criteria: Each move shows the two operands interacting and the result emerging; animation does not block subsequent input.
close_reason: Destination tile glyph flies into the dot, result pops in with scale animation, delta indicator (↑ +n / ↓ n / — ±0 / ✕ invalid) rises, status number flashes up/down/flat. CSS-transition based, does not block input (verified rapid successive keypresses in jsdom).

description: Make the h1 title on play.html a link to index.html, styled as plain text.
